newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sugar, Formosa Plastics in oil joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sugar, Formosa Plastics in oil joint venture.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp said on Wednesday it had decided to form a T$800 million joint venture with petrochemical giant Formosa Plastics Corp in a bid to enter the island's liberalising oil market.
Taiwan Sugar spokesman Cheng Hung-tsai said his firm and Formosa Plastics planned to build nine oil products storage units in southern Kaohsiung.
Formosa Plastics will take 55 percent of the venture, with Taiwan Sugar holding the rest, Cheng said by telephone.
The nine storage units are four unleaded gasoline units with capacities of 188,000 barrels, three diesel units of 94,000 barrels and two jet fuel units with 63,000 barrels.
He did not give a timetable for the construction.
Cheng said Taiwan Sugar also planned to build 80 to 100 petrol stations island-wide within five years.
Taiwan's Energy Commission announced a lifting of curbs on oil imports on June 26, but other regulations prevent any private imports before 1999.
A qualifying clause in the oil import regulation limits oil import volume to less than 50 percent of an importer's annual oil production.
Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp remains the island's only oil products producer and the only importer.
Formosa Plastics is building a US$10.8 billion refinery and petrochemical complex by 1999.
